comment: Size-marker vocabulary. One source, three consumers:
tools/review/scales.mjs    — builds the SCALES.md / SCALES.html report, a section per entry;
tools/review/px-audit.mjs  — the gate: a px literal with no marker does not pass
tests/base-size-markers.test.ts  — the same scan over the shared layer scss/widgets/base/**, against a baseline: that layer cannot be marked in one go, so the count only ratchets down.
The report and the gate cannot drift: this list is the only one.
Fields: id — section anchor; marker — the token in a `// <marker>: note` comment;
title/question/why — section copy; literals — what counts as a distinct value in the summary
(px — pixels only, any — any literal with a unit, steps — step names);
scale — the package scale family the report looks the value up in (null — do not look up);

categories.title: A. Sizes off the scales
categories.question: which values deserve a step
categories.why: A named theme size with no matching step in any relevant package scale: the value stayed a px literal.

categories.title: B. Step exists, role does not
categories.question: which steps deserve semantic roles
categories.why: The value sits on a base scale step, but the package has no semantic role for this case — the theme reads the base scale directly.

categories.title: B2. Icon glyph sizes
categories.question: does the package need an icon size scale
categories.why: A glyph is sized by a font-size step or by a fraction of the font size: the package has no icon scale of its own.

categories.title: C. Proportional values
categories.question: do proportional values need DS roles
categories.why: The value is proportional to the font size or to the container. It cannot become an absolute token without changing behaviour: em is measured from the element's font size, a token from the root.

categories.title: D. Computed sizes
categories.question: what to compute at build time and what at runtime
categories.why: A token arrives in CSS as var(), so Sass can no longer fold the arithmetic: derived values move to the browser.

categories.title: E. Pixel nudges
categories.question: should the correction follow the scale or stay absolute
categories.why: An absolute addition or subtraction on top of a token. When the scale moves the derived value follows and the correction does not — on a large step ±1px goes unnoticed, on a small one it is a visible fraction of the size.

categories.title: F. Shadow geometry
categories.question: a shadow role as a whole, rather than steps for its numbers
categories.why: Offset, blur and spread inside box-shadow. The package ships shadow geometry as px tokens of its own, so the question is not which step but whether a shadow role is wanted — the theme already takes the shadow colour from a role.

categories.title: G. Border and line thickness
categories.question: put them on border-width steps, or must a hairline stay 1px
categories.why: The thickness of a border, of a hairline drawn with box-shadow, or of a strip revealed by clip-path. A matching step exists (border-width-10 = 1px), but a hairline is not meant to thicken along with the scale.

categories.title: H. Must stay a number
categories.question: no decision needed — the value is frozen by the technique
categories.why: A @media or @container condition: var() is invalid there, so the value cannot become a token even once a step exists. When the step moves the condition stays where it is — worth knowing in advance.

categories.title: I. Fixed sizes written into rules
categories.question: does it deserve a step, or does the size stay fixed
categories.why: The number is written where it applies — in a rule, a mixin argument or a derived variable — with no name of its own. Unlike A, a step with that value usually does exist: the step column shows which one.

categories.title: J. Sizes owned by the shared layer
categories.question: does the theme get a knob, or does the number stay shared
categories.why: A value in scss/widgets/base/** that every theme compiles. The marker is the record of a decision by the base owners: the number is the same for generic, material, fluent and fluent-next, and opening a knob for one theme would buy nothing. Base-layer marker: in the theme itself there is no shared layer to own a value, so a theme literal marked this way is a mistake.

categories.title: K. Not a designed size
categories.question: no decision needed — the number is a technique, not a size
categories.why: An off-screen parking coordinate (top: -9999px), a one-pixel probe, a number chosen to be far outside the viewport rather than to be seen. Nobody designs it and no step can replace it: making it a token would only invite someone to tune it. Unlike H, the value is not frozen by a syntax — it is frozen by having no visual meaning.
